reason: I tried to kill this on the brief's own hypothesis - that .tl-device is a phone chassis and .tl-paperEdge a sheet of paper, both legitimately white on both grounds - and the pixels refuse it. WHAT REPRODUCES, exactly, sampled at 1440x960 on the composited screenshot: on ?v=ink the .tl-device edge is rgb(217,217,217) in phone, day, ended, loading and loading-slow, with rgb(17,17,17) 6px outside it AND rgb(17,17,17) 6px inside it - 13.38:1 against both. On ?v=ink desk the .tl-paperEdge is rgb(255,255,255), 18.88:1, byte-identical to --fore. On ?v=paper the same two read 217 (1.31:1) and 217 (1.29:1), and print reads 231 on BOTH grounds because print forces paper. Every figure in the finding lands. THE REPRESENTATIONAL DEFENCE DIES ON THE INSIDE PIXEL. `background: var(--paper)` on these two elements paints zero visible area: .b-field is the sole child and carries `background: var(--back)`, measured rgb(17,17,17) 6px inside the edge on ink. So the white is not a chassis and not a sheet - it is a 1px stroke with an invisible white substrate underneath it, a compositing accident, not a body. A white phone has a chassis you can see; this has a face of #111 with a bright rim. The same test kills the 'sheet of paper on a desk' reading: the sheet's face measures #111. THE LAB ALREADY DOES THIS CORRECTLY, AND SAYS SO. b.css 1052-1085 marks the chat card 'LITERAL, not laddered: the chat app is somebody else's surface' and builds it right - on ink publish .b-chatPlate measures border 255 over interior 255, so the rim is absorbed by its own white card and does nothing, which is how a genuinely white object behaves. Neither .tl-device nor .tl-paperEdge carries any such note; the only comment on .tl-device explains WHEN it is drawn, never its colour. THE INLINE PATCH IS THE PROOF OF INTENT AND IT IS INVERTED. states.desk writes `border-color:var(--fore-16)` explicitly, which is only meaningful if the edge is supposed to flip with the ground. Unpatched, ink desk would composite to 231 (~15.2:1); patched it composites to 255 (18.88:1). The team's own fix made the ink room louder because the white beneath it was never touched. LOOKED AT, NOT ONLY MEASURED: ink-desk--1440x960.png is a pure-white 1px rectangle around the whole artifact, running off the bottom of the viewport - the brightest continuous element on the page, at the same white as the 148px count, on a page whose one accent (indigo rail) sits at 3.00:1 and whose every hairline sits at 1.59:1. That is not a phone at night; it is a box. FIX VERIFIED BY INJECTION AND RE-SHOT: paper phone 217 and print 231 (both grounds) come back byte-identical; ink device edge -> rgb(55,55,55) (1.59:1, the lab's ordinary hairline) and the phone still reads as a bounded device, the desk frame stops being a white box. TWO CORRECTIONS the seat should carry, neither fatal: (1) 'the only two objects still written against literal ink and paper' is loose - b.css 1056-1135 (.b-chat, .b-bubble, .b-unfurl, .b-og) is also literal, and shell.css body/.tl-page hardcode var(--paper) as the alpha-wash substrate. Both are documented and correct. The true claim is 'the only two UNDOCUMENTED ones, and the only two whose literal fill contradicts their own laddered edge'. (2) The finding's verification numbers for paper desk (231) and ink desk (41) come from an injection that used !important and so overrode the inline patch it says to keep; with the patch kept, paper desk stays 217 (i.e. unchanged from today, which is 217 not 231) and ink desk lands at 55, not 41. Substance unaffected. This is a two-line correction inside a frozen structure, it costs nothing on the shipping paper room, and it removes the one object in the ink room that is louder than the design.
sharpenedFix: shell.css 279-289: `.tl-device { border: 1px solid var(--fore-16); background: var(--back); }` and `.tl-paperEdge { border: 1px solid var(--fore-10); background: var(--back); }`. KEEP the inline `border-color:var(--fore-16)` on .tl-paperEdge in render-b.js states.desk - with the background now the ground it is finally doing what it was written to do, and it is what holds paper desk at its present 217. Expect, re-sampled: paper phone 217 (unchanged), paper desk 217 (unchanged), print 231 on both grounds (unchanged, print forces paper), ink device edge 55 (13.38:1 -> 1.59:1), ink desk edge 55 (18.88:1 -> 1.59:1). Rebuild with build.mjs. Add one assertion to interaction-check.mjs, phrased against composited pixels rather than computed style, since computed style is exactly what hid this: for each room and each state, take whichever of .tl-device / .tl-paperEdge is present, screenshot, sample the border pixel at the left edge at mid-height and the page pixel 4px outside it, and require the WCAG ratio between them below 2:1 on both grounds. Sampling only the outside pixel is enough and avoids the rounded corners; do not assert on print, which forces paper by design.
